The 157-second figure predates that fix. The §18.2 trigger ("the first projection measured too slow as a fold") fired once; whether it still holds is the re-measurement at the end of 0.3.0: profile a drain start and `clutch status` on this repo's journal (now 14 segments, about 27k lines) and record the share of wall time in journal reads. If it is under a quarter, the window slides and this plan waits for the next measurement.
docs/journal-sql-refactor-plan.md:40:What the incremental reader did not change: 101 call sites still fold whole event lists in Python; `clutch/observe.py:254-256` has its own raw segment reader that returns dicts and wraps them in `SimpleNamespace` four times to call Event-typed helpers; `clutch/scheduler.py:80` reaches into `journal.dir.parent`, `journal._fs`, and `journal._clock`; and the roadmap's audit found the same "latest state for stem" scan written inline 13 times (`docs/roadmap.md` §2.1 row 5). Those are the costs a query layer removes whether or not the read time still dominates; the 0.3.0 ticket `journal-last-transition-helper` removes the worst of them without the dependency.
